title: E-Signatures Are Coming to Dossie

meta_description: E-signatures are on the Dossie roadmap for a Q2 2026 beta. Here's what's being built: send for signature inside the dossier, with role-based prefill.
deck: Not shipped yet. E-signatures are on the roadmap for a Q2 2026 beta — here's what she'll do when they land.

intro_html: E-signatures are not live yet. They're listed on Dossie's roadmap as a Q2 2026 beta, and nothing on this page is available in your account today. It's here so you know what's being built and can tell us whether it's the right shape. Until it ships, Dossie files the signed copies you send through your existing e-sign tool.

steps.p: The plan: any document already in the dossier — amendment, addendum, disclosure — gets sent for signature from the same place it lives, instead of exporting it first.

Dossie already knows who's the buyer's agent and who's the seller's agent on a file, so the intent is to prefill the right recipient with the right fields rather than dragging signature boxes onto a PDF by hand.
The goal is for the executed copy to land back in the dossier on its own once every party has signed — no download-and-reupload step.

callout: Timing: Q2 2026 beta, priced at $0.50 per envelope as an add-on. Dates on a roadmap are intentions, not commitments — we'll say so plainly here if they move.
cta_title: Dossie is worth having before e-sign lands.
cta_sub: Contract scanning, TREC deadlines cited to the paragraph, and drafted follow-ups all work today. E-signatures join them in the Q2 2026 beta.

faq.q: Can I send a document for signature in Dossie today?
faq.a: No. E-signatures are not released yet — they're on the roadmap for a Q2 2026 beta. Keep using your current e-sign tool and upload the executed copy to the dossier; Dossie files and reads it like any other document.
The current target is a Q2 2026 beta, offered as a $0.50-per-envelope add-on. That's a plan, not a promise — if the date moves, this page moves with it.

faq.q: Will I need a separate e-signature account?
faq.a: The intent is no — Send for Signature is being built to run inside Dossie, so there's no second tool to log into. That's the design goal, not a shipped feature.

legal_note: The screen shown here is a design preview of an unreleased feature, not a shipped Dossie screen. E-signatures are not available in Dossie today.
